question: Under Article 7(1)(e) of Directive 2006/126/EC, driving licences are to be issued to applicants who are normally resident in the Member State issuing the licence, or who can produce evidence that they have been studying there for at least six months. This can be challenging for cross-border commuters who live in one Member State but work and follow vocational training in another.

This is the case, for example, in transport and logistics, where driving licences for heavy goods vehicles are a necessary part of the training. People may thus have worked in a Member State for several years, but are nevertheless unable to obtain their driving licence there because they have been in training for less than six months. With the above in mind: 1.

How should the six-month requirement be interpreted when it comes to cross-border commuters who are in vocational training but already have long-term links with the Member State concerned through their work?
Can previous residence and employment be included in the assessment, or is the sixmonth period counted only from the start of the training?
Does the Commission think that Directive (EU) 2025/2205 is clear enough, or is further guidance needed to make sure there are no obstacles standing in the way of cross-border vocational training?
